extracted.intended_audience: improv and sketch performers/students (UCB Training Center attendees, teachers, and writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and performing improvised scenes and writing sketches focused on identifying the scene's 'game' and heightening it logically; aimed at performers and students learning UCB pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game as center of pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: UCB pedagogy organizes around finding and playing the GAME of a scene. A game is the first specific, repeatable, unusual element identified in a scene. Once found, all subsequent moves heighten that game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center scene choices on discovering the first specific, repeatable, unusual element; let subsequent moves heighten that identified game rather than introducing unrelated jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern Game
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern Game — a behavior repeats with variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a recognizable repeating behavior and vary it each time to build comedic expectation and surprise; use variation to escalate or complicate the pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV Game
rubrics_metrics.description: POV Game — a character has an unusual point of view, applied across situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain an unusual point of view for a character across different situations so the clash between that POV and the situation creates comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status/Reality Game
rubrics_metrics.description: Status/Reality Game — an unusual social structure is treated as normal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and commit to an altered social structure or reality (e.g., reversed status dynamics) and treat it as normal to reveal comedic tension through character responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: If-Then logic
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the world is X, THEN logically Y follows. The improviser's job is to find the funniest LOGICAL implication, not the funniest random thing. Random escalation breaks the audience's investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical consequences of the established world to heighten scenes. Prioritize causes-and-effects that naturally follow from the premise rather than unrelated gag escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong initiations contain a who, where, what, AND a hint of relationship. Avoid declaring the game in the initiation; let it emerge. A declarative line of dialogue is stronger than a question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open scenes by grounding basic facts (who/where/what) and implying relationships; resist stating the game's mechanics outright; prefer declarative statements to establish reality and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing scenes (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit when the laugh peaks, not after. Sweeps mid-laugh teach the team trust. A scene that goes 30 seconds past its peak is unrecoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut at the laugh peak to maintain momentum and teach ensemble trust; use 'sweeps' during laughs when appropriate; avoid letting a scene continue long after its strongest laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch as logical extension of scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketches are scenes with the game pre-identified. The sketch's job: heighten the game systematically across acts. Each beat must complicate, not repeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing sketches, identify the game up front and structure beats to systematically heighten that game across acts; ensure each beat adds complication or stakes rather than mere repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: identify the game in first 30 seconds
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you identified the game in the first 30 seconds?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the game's element is established quickly so the audience can track the logic and heightening from early in the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: heightening via if-then
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you heightening through if-then logic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that each escalation follows logically from the established premise (if X, then Y) rather than relying on unrelated surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: vertical/horizontal/thematic heightening
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the heightening vertical, horizontal, or thematic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be intentional about the mode of escalation: vertical (increase intensity), horizontal (add variations), or thematic (deepen the concept/theme) and choose which best serves the game.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: initiations declarative and grounded
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm initiations state facts and ground the scene (who/where/what/relationship) with declarative lines rather than tentative questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: edit at the laugh peak
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you editing at the laugh peak?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor audience or scene laughter and plan edits (cuts/sweeps) at the peak to preserve momentum and avoid deflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: UCB Working Rubric: each beat should complicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Is each beat complicating, not just repeating?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design beats so they add complications or new information that advances the game; avoid beats that merely repeat earlier material without escalation.
